passage:
The secret of Yesterday Hills
‘Is that it?’ Janice leaned over Perry for a
better view as the little twin-engine plane
began another descent.
‘You ask that every time we put down,’
Perry grumbled. ‘There’s another
hour yet.’

they had left Melbourne that morning
and changed at Brisbane for their stay
in south-west Queensland. Then we’d
be jetting to London, instead of some
crummy little town beyond the black
stump—wherever that is!

‘I don’t think I’ll get out this time for a bit
of a stretch,’ Janice yawned.

‘You’ll love it,’ their parents had said,
‘seeing more of Australia. We can’t take
you with us. It’s a business trip.’

When the plane took off again only
three passengers remained, men in
wide-brimmed hats. Bits of conversation
drifted down the aisle. ‘Over 20 000
head . . . if this drought keeps up . . .
heartbreak corner . . . ’

Six months, Janice thought bleakly. With
some great-aunt we haven’t seen since
we were babies. Some old witch woman
who’ll forget to turn on her hearing aid,
I bet.

Separated by the narrow aisle, the twins
stared glumly out at the few wisps of
clouds. They tuned in silently to each
other’s thoughts, out of habit.

Witch woman! Perry grinned as the twins’
thoughts tuned in to each other again.
He wasn’t too worried about some old
great-aunt. But a new school . . . Perry
was frowning.

They could have taken us, Perry was
thinking for the umpteenth time since

from The Secret of Yesterday Hills
by Elsie Young
HBJ 1990

questions.stem: Why were Janice and Perry on the plane?
options: They had to stay with a great-aunt while their parents went to London.
The drought had made it too difficult to stay at home.
It was a chance to escape from their great-aunt.
They were off to meet their parents.

questions.stem: What was special about Janice and Perry?
options: They knew all about their parents’ business.
They were allowed to travel without their parents.
They could cope with a wicked great-aunt.

questions.stem:
Choose the correct option to complete the sentence.
The other passengers travelling on the plane with the twins were [Choose 1…] .
options: cattle graziers / tourists / relatives / school teachers

questions.stem: How does the reader know that the trip from Brisbane onwards was long and tiring? Choose two options.
options: Janice did not want to leave the plane one more time to stretch her legs.
Janice and Perry were getting bored with the endless view of wispy clouds.
The plane flew over land that was very dry and monotonous.
Most of the passengers had left the plane.
The small plane had made many descents and landings.

questions.stem:
Click on the word that tells you about the twins’ emotions.
Separated by the narrow aisle, the twins stared glumly out at the few wisps of clouds.
questions.notes: each word is a clickable button

questions.stem: How did Perry react to Janice’s idea that their great-aunt was a witch woman?
options: He started to have doubts about their safety.
He wondered why Janice was being nasty.
He was upset by Janice’s unfair criticism of an old lady.
He was impressed by the description.
